newsitem.title: SWEDEN: More Swedish households see higher inflation-poll.
newsitem.headline: More Swedish households see higher inflation-poll.

text.p: Swedish households are increasingly expecting an increase in inflation over the coming year, according to the latest survey by pollster SKOP released on Thursday.
The monthly survey found 18.7 percent of households surveyed expected inflation to increase over the coming year compared to 18 percent in SKOP's last poll in January.
But Swedish households were less pessimistic about their own economies for the second consecutive month, the poll found.
The survey conducted over February/March found 23.1 percent of households expected their own living standards to suffer in the coming year compared to 27.2 percent in Janauary.
The number that believed their living standards would increase also fell to 13.6 percent from 13.7 percent.
The SKOP poll found that the number of households expecting the country's economic situation to worsen rose to 41 percent from 38.7 percent.
Only 21.4 percent expected to see an improvement in the economy against 24.2 percent in the previous poll.
